title: Private Deploy: Onboarding, Failover, and Rollback Runbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:

This runbook documents the recommended end-to-end onboarding, failover, and rollback procedures for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for field engineers, SREs, and customer platform owners. The goal is to provide a single canonical reference that covers: network & KMS prerequisites, installation checks, day-2 observability and operational playbooks, safe upgrade flows, and explicit rollback steps for stateful components.

Scope:
- Applies to Private deployments using Redwood control plane (hybrid or private-control options) and on-prem runtime installs (air-gapped and networked).
- Covers tenant onboarding through full-service acceptance, plus in-place upgrades and emergency rollback for runtime, model artifacts, and KV/embedding stores.
- Excludes: internal hosted API procedures and purely cloud-native managed Dedicated contracts.

Owners and escalation path:
- Primary owner: Private Deployments Engineering (oncall: private-deploy-team@redwood.com)
- Secondary owner: SRE (oncall: eng-sre@redwood.com)
- Escalation: PagerDuty -> Private Deploy Lead -> Platform Security -> CTO on critical incidents

SLOs and thresholds relevant to runbook:
- Service availability (per-tenant): 99.95% monthly for control-plane endpoints
- Inference P99 latency objective: 250ms for 512-token model baseline when on dedicated capacity
- Acceptable post-upgrade error spike: <0.5% anomalous error rate sustained over 30m

Prerequisites and customer requirements checklist (summary table):
| Area | Minimum requirement | Responsible party | Notes |
|------|---------------------|-------------------|-------|
| Network | BGP/VPC peering or private interconnect + NAT egress | Customer | /24 inbound for service endpoints; mTLS recommended |
| KMS | Customer KMS reachable from control plane (TLS 1.3) | Customer + Redwood | Support: AWS KMS, Vault HSM. Rotation window: 30d |
| Storage | NFS/SMB or S3-compatible object storage for model artifacts | Customer | Min IOPS 500 for model loads; signed URL support required |
| GPUs | Node labels for GPU type and driver >= 525.xx | Customer | Use curated driver matrix (see Appendix) |
| Telemetry | Metrics + traces exported to permitted collector | Customer/Redwood | Default retention 30d; sampling 1% for traces |

Network topologies and recommended segmentation:
- Trusted control plane (customer-managed network): keep control-plane management subnets isolated from inference data plane.
- Recommended subnet layout (example):
  1. management-subnet (10.10.0.0/24) — control-plane APIs, admin access
  2. runtime-subnet (10.10.1.0/22) — inference pods, GPUs, model caches
  3. telemetry-subnet (10.10.4.0/24) — exporters, log-forwarders, metrics ingest
- Egress rules: allow outbound to Redwood control-plane endpoints (if hybrid), KMS endpoints, and object storage. Block wide open egress from runtime nodes.

Onboarding checklist (high level):
1. Validate customer prerequisites (network ranges, KMS endpoint, storage access).
2. Exchange and verify certs and trust anchors.
3. Bootstrap control plane components (namespace creation, serviceaccounts, CRDs).
4. Run smoke tests: health checks for control plane, runtime connectivity, and KMS decrypt cycle.
5. Deploy initial runtime (small capacity), run load smoke: 50 concurrent requests for 1 hour.
6. Acceptance testing with customer's sample workloads and perf tests.
7. Sign-off and handover to customer operations with runbook and contact list.

Example CLI & health checks (illustrative):
- Verify control plane reachable:
  curl -k https://$CONTROL_PLANE_URL/healthz
- KMS decrypt test (openssl via TLS endpoint):
  echo "test" | openssl s_client -connect kms.example.com:443 -quiet
- Runtime pod readiness (Kubernetes):
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=runtime -o wide

Day-2 operational procedures:
- Routine checks (daily):
  - Control-plane API 2xx rate > 99%
  - Model manifest sync time < 5m
  - Storage latency (S3/obj) P95 < 200ms
- Incident triage (short):
  1. Confirm impact: which tenants, which model, degradations (latency/errors).
  2. Scope: control plane vs runtime vs network vs KMS.
  3. If KMS errors, immediately route to cached fallback key (if configured) and notify security.
- Scaling and autoscaling guidance:
  - Preferred: horizontal pod autoscaler with conservative min/max bounds.
  - For burst events: pre-warm model caches using background preload job (example: workload-warmup cron).

Upgrade strategy (stateful-aware):
- Principles: small batches, canary-first, health gating, observable rollback markers.
- Components impacted: control-plane API, runtime agents, model artifacts, KV caches, GPU drivers.

Planned upgrade flow (recommended):
1. Create a rollout plan document with target versions and candidate hosts in a release channel.
2. Snapshot critical state: KV store backup, blob store object list, and model version map.
   - Commands: snapshots via etcdctl or configured KV backup tool; ensure backups stored off-node.
3. Canary deploy to 1-2 nodes (non-production tenant traffic). Monitor for 60 minutes:
   - Metrics: request success rate, tail latency, OOM events, GPU driver errors.
4. If canary passes, roll forward to 10% of capacity. Repeat checks at 30m intervals.
5. Full rollout in progressive waves with automated health gating.
6. Post-upgrade validation: run a synthetic prompt suite comparing generation quality and token counts.

Emergency rollback procedure (stateful safe path):
- When to rollback: persistent P99 latency breach > 20% baseline for 30m OR error rates > 2% sustained for 15m AND canary checks failed.
- Rollback constraints: model artifacts and KV state are the main risk vectors. Follow these steps: 
  1. Halt new model loads and stop traffic to affected nodes (use traffic router to rehome).
  2. Promote pre-upgrade snapshot as authoritative: restore KV snapshot to a staging cluster and validate checksums.
  3. Re-deploy previous runtime artifacts (OCI images) using pinned manifests.
     kubectl -n redwood set image deployment/runtime runtime=registry.redwood.com/runtime:stable-old
  4. Reattach model object store pointers (restore object-level manifests if any were changed).
  5. Gradually reintroduce traffic to nodes, monitoring for regressions.
  6. Open a rollback incident ticket with timeline and backup references.

Safe rollback checklist (quick):
- Backup verified and available off-node
- KV snapshot integrity checked (checksum match)
- Model artifact list restored and accessible by runtime
- GPU driver compatibility confirmed with old runtime image

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- KMS handshake failures after upgrade: revert KMS client library, or use emergency cached key path.
- Model mismatch errors (artifact schema change): restore previous manifest and force model reload.
- Persistent OOM on GPU nodes: scale up instance type or reduce batch sizes; roll back to previous runtime with different memory profile.

Audit and post-incident review steps:
1. Capture timeline of changes, metrics, and logs (centralized archive).
2. Run regression-eval on example prompts to quantify behavioral drift.
3. Produce short RCA and action items with owners and deadlines.
4. Update this runbook with any new lessons and add tests to the eval harness.

Appendix: sample configuration snippets
- Example HPA snippet (Kubernetes):
  apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
  kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
  metadata:
    name: runtime-hpa
    namespace: redwood
  spec:
    scaleTargetRef:
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      name: runtime
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 20
    metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 65

- Example KV backup command (etcdctl example):
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /backups/etcd-snap-$(date +%F).db --endpoints=$ETCD_ENDPOINTS 

Appendix: driver and binary compatibility matrix (short):
| Runtime image tag | Required NVIDIA driver | Notes |
|-------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| runtime:stable-old | 515.xx | Legacy quant kernels |
| runtime:2026-01-rc | 525.xx | New attention kernel opt-in |
